native_error_contract: Texture2d::blit observes unchanged Blitter::new (both shader/pipeline programs, sampler/layouts), native encoder creation and actual Blitter::blit bind/pass/draw operations under one immediate observation. View.clear likewise observes encoder creation and pass lifetime including drop before closure returns.

Both closure operations are infallible in their Rust return shape and contain no ?/early application Err. observe_validation always pops after normal completion and returns the first actual native Validation cause. Thus no nested body-primary/secondary resolver is needed here; genuine native Rust panic/unwind is not converted into an invented application error.

An observed error prevents submission of that encoder and returns ComputePassError::Native(Arc<actual wgpu::Error>). Existing Error::source exposes the original native object. Any deferred finish error and subsequent queue error are separately observed by unchanged WgpuContext::submit. Neither stage waits for completion or promises rollback of prior native work.

Immediate observer pushes/pop only on native contexts with blocking_validation enabled. It contains no device.poll or GPU completion wait. Browser/borrowed modes retain configured provider error handling and no synchronous validation verdict; non-Validation classes retain native handling.

No new GPU state/cache publication or callbacks are introduced. Local Arc clones keep view/device lifetime through the call. No source/native allocation port is newly required for cached-view clear/blit.
